div.div:
Definition: An object that acts as a Gateway to a database table. One instance handles all the rows in the table.
• Data Structure: Returns untyped tabular recordsets (DataSets, Arrays of Maps, Knex query results).
• Synergy: Ideal match for Table Module and transaction-script-heavy batch pipelines.
• Limitations: Awkward with polymorphic objects; does not encapsulate domain invariants.

div.div:
Definition: An object that acts as a Gateway to a single record in a data source. One instance per row.
• Data Structure: Strongly typed properties mirroring table columns exactly (getters/setters, update(), delete()).
• Separation: Isolates SQL access code from domain logic; business logic lives in separate domain objects.
• Limitations: High boilerplate; creates duplicate class hierarchies (Domain Entity + Row Gateway).

div.div:
Definition: An object that wraps a database row, encapsulates database access, and adds domain logic.
• Sweet Spot: Rapid application development, straightforward CRUD, simple domain invariants.
• The Trap at Scale: Domain entities are hardcoded to database tables. Business rules become deeply entangled with ORM query builders, making unit testing impossible without mocking database connections.
• Violation: Violates Single Responsibility Principle (Domain Logic + SQL persistence).

div.div:
Definition: A layer of mappers that moves data between objects and a database while keeping them independent of each other and the mapper itself.
• Complete Decoupling: Domain entities are pure TypeScript/Java POJOs. Zero SQL, zero ORM decorator leakages. Invariants are self-protecting and testable in pure in-memory unit tests.
• Coordination: Pairs with Unit of Work and Identity Map for transactional batch execution.
• Trade-off: Higher initial architectural complexity; requires explicit mapping configuration.
